newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota panel advances $51 mln arena bond bill.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota panel advances $51 mln arena bond bill.

text.p: A Minnesota House committee on Thursday approved a proposal to sell $51 million of bonds to renovate a St. Paul arena with an eye toward landing a National Hockey League franchise.

But whether or not St. Paul lands an NHL expansion team, or one seeking to relocate, Mayor Norm Coleman believes that the 25-year-old Civic Center is due for an overhaul, spokesman Paul Adelmann said.

St. Paul and five other U.S. cities have been chosen as finalists for an NHL expansion franchise. Both St. Paul and Minneapolis officials also have expressed interest in landing the Hartford Whalers franchise which plans to leave Connecticut at the end of this season.

NHL Commissioner Gary Bettman and the league's expansion committee members met with St. Paul officials and toured the arena on Wednesday. They also met with representatives from Columbus, Ohio, another finalist, on Wednesday.
The proposal passed out of the House Local Government and Metropolitan Affairs Committee and must undergo further consideration from House committees.

Minnesota is in a non-bonding year for its biennium budgeting process, but the committee members "just wanted to get it out there on the table and to have it there ready to go to indicate (to the NHL) that it is a place where hockey ought to be," said Bob DeBoer, spokesman for Rep. Ann Rest, D-New Hope, who chairs the committee.

If approved, the renovation would include adding luxury boxes, new seating and exteriors. The proposal to issue general obligation debt has the support of Gov. Arne Carlson, who also favors a $5.5 million appropriation to begin renovations this year.
